# The negation of an interval, one-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_neg_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An interval $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ that contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, with $X = [x_l, x_u]$. An interval may be unbounded, and empty.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, -x : x \in X \,\}.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **I1.** The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- **I2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ is.
- **I3.** $Z$ contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, unbounded operands included (their members are real numbers).
- **I4.** For nonempty $X$, where $\ell$ and $h$ are the greatest lower bound and the least upper bound of the exact range $\{\, -x : x \in X \,\}$, as extended real numbers: $z_l = \ell$ and $z_u = h$, exactly.
- **I5.** For bounded $X$, $Z$ is bounded exactly when every member $z$ of the exact range satisfies $\lvert z\rvert \le \Omega$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_neg_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeInterval1.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeInterval1.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_neg_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_neg_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the bounds negated and exchanged (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_neg_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_neg_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The negation of an interval with one-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "One
# limb"): exact; the empty set (+inf, -inf) is its own negation. Bounded exactly when the operand
# is, which for a bounded operand is that every member of -X is within Omega. For every precision.

zl = neg(xu)
zu = neg(xl)
```
